memory_update.text: New Hotspots should be treated as a cross-sector chokepoint funnel: policy shocks plus demand acceleration can reveal shared upstream constraints before standard sector labels capture them.
Tungsten APT/WF6 remains the cleanest hidden bottleneck lane because it connects semiconductors, tooling and defense through one intermediate processing stage.
AI data-center power should be decomposed into switchgear, transformers, cooling, interconnection and EPC rather than only GPU demand.
HBM/advanced packaging should be researched one layer below the producers, especially tools, inspection, test and gas-handling subsystems.
Sulphur/sulphuric-acid and marine biofouling/coatings are important theme branches but still lack strong public-company mapping in the supplied evidence set.

summary: Merged and deduplicated the Layer 1 universe for New Hotspots into a cross-sector chokepoint map. The strongest evidence-backed lanes in the supplied context are tungsten/APT/WF6, AI data-center power, HBM/advanced packaging, and nuclear fuel; sulphur/sulphuric acid and marine biofouling remain important theme branches but are still under-mapped at the public-company level. The universe intentionally keeps both reference leaders and underfollowed second-order names so later layers can test bottlenecks, customer linkage, and valuation/pricing dislocations.
